title: Coherent normalization of strict reduction compact-support exchanges
statement:
Fix the finite-field and integral coefficient conventions of [def-pur-conventions], with $R=\mathcal O_E$, $P_n=R/\varpi_E^n$, and completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat R_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes and let $a:Y'\to Y$ and $b:Y''\to Y'$ be arbitrary scheme maps for which all pullback squares and operation composites lie in the supplied domains of [fix-lem-exchanges]. Supply a compactification $c=(j,p)$ and its successive pullbacks [def-weil-compactifications-refinements, pur713-def-base-changed-compactification]. All open factors are quasi-compact. Let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$ have the compatible finite etale-origin witnesses required on these domains. Write $\mathcal R_T$ for the actual strict quotient-reduction functor with its quotient transitions, and $\operatorname{Res}_T$ for termwise restriction along $\underline R_T\to\widehat R_T$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Let $w_a$ be the specified strict compact-support exchange: the proper strict lift $v'_\bullet$ followed by the strict finite open-extension comparison that defines [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map]; the integral open factor is normalized by its finite reduction diagrams as in [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. In constant-$R$ tower coordinates use $G_t,R_t^{\mathcal T},J_j$ of [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations, def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension], and put
$$H_a^{\mathcal T}=(R_{p_a}^{\mathcal T}\beta_a)\circ(E_{p,a}^{\mathcal T}J_j),$$
where $E^{\mathcal T}$ is the proper pullback-square mate and $\beta_a:G_{\bar a}J_j\cong J_{j_a}G_{a_X}$ is the open-unit-normalized map [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. There are specified natural source and target identifications $\kappa_{a,s},\kappa_{a,t}$ from the restricted strict corners of $w_a$ to those of $H_a^{\mathcal T}$: on the proper factors they are the $b,d$ of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization], and on the open factors they are the canonical pullback/reduction tensor and open-extension identifications. They satisfy
$$\kappa_{a,t}\circ\operatorname{Res}(w_a)=H_a^{\mathcal T}\circ\kappa_{a,s}$$
in the derived strict constant-tower category. The identifications for $a,b,a\circ b$ intertwine the canonical pullback compositors, so the two successive substitutions have identical intermediate corner maps. The same identifications carry the strict refinement comparisons to the normalized constant-tower comparisons, with their cocycle and exchange-intertwining equations [lem-cbc-complete-proetale-refinement-exchange-coherence]. All these assertions concern simultaneous diagram-site maps and their quotient transitions before $R\lim$ or finite evaluation; they include underlying scheme maps semilinear over $k$ and require no $k$-linearity.

proof.text: Work throughout on the small strict diagram sites, and put $\overline M=\operatorname{Res}_X\mathcal R_X(M)$. Use the canonical coefficient identifications along every edge. They respect the finite projections, quotient transitions, identities and scheme-map composition [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. The completed ring is flat over the constant ring and the quotient-reduction/scalar comparisons respect quotient transitions [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Consequently the exact restriction and the normalized derived direct-image comparisons on these diagram sites are those of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction]; in particular they preserve adjuncts, units and counits. This fixes one set of corner maps, rather than selecting maps from finite evaluations.

source.place: Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change); coefficient/scalar diagram refinements are the cited DAG statements

proof.text: First identify the open input. The strict isomorphism $\rho_j:\mathcal R_{\overline X}(j_!M)\simeq j_!\mathcal R_X(M)$ is [lem-cbc-ringed-open-strict-reduction]. Restrict it and then use the open scalar comparison $e:\operatorname{Res}j_!\simeq J_j\operatorname{Res}$ of [lem-cbc-ringed-open-scalar-adjunction]; denote the resulting map by $z_j:\operatorname{Res}\mathcal R_{\overline X}(j_!M)\simeq J_j\overline M$. Both comparisons preserve the open unit and the quotient augmentation. The quasi-compactness stipulated for $j$ and the completeness of $M$ give completeness of $j_!M$ by [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison]. Its finite origin witnesses are among the supplied intermediate witnesses in the statement. Thus the proper normalization theorem can be applied to $K=j_!M$, including after either supplied base change.

source.place: Tags 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), 03DJ (lemma-extension-by-zero-exact), with the cited strict-reduction and completeness refinements

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-tower-exchange-mate-normalization] to the proper square $(p,p_a,a,\bar a)$ and $K=j_!M$. For its specified strict proper corners $B_a,D_a$, write the prescribed maps as $b_a:\operatorname{Res}B_a\simeq G_aR_p^{\mathcal T}\operatorname{Res}\mathcal R(K)$ and $d_a:\operatorname{Res}D_a\simeq R_{p_a}^{\mathcal T}G_{\bar a}\operatorname{Res}\mathcal R(K)$. Its actual equality is $d_a\operatorname{Res}(v'_a)=E_{p,a}^{\mathcal T}b_a$. Define $\kappa_{a,s}=G_aR_p^{\mathcal T}(z_j)b_a$ and, for now, $\widetilde\kappa_{a,m}=R_{p_a}^{\mathcal T}G_{\bar a}(z_j)d_a$. Naturality of the proper mate, applied to $z_j$, gives $\widetilde\kappa_{a,m}\operatorname{Res}(v'_a)=(E_{p,a}^{\mathcal T}J_j)\kappa_{a,s}$. The theorem identifies the specified lift itself, before evaluation.

source.place: Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change), proper strict-mate normalization as stated in the cited node

proof.text: For the upper open square, [lem-cbc-completed-open-strict-mate-identification] gives $z_{a,t}\operatorname{Res}(\omega_a)=\beta_a z_{a,s}$, with the specified pullback/reduction and open-extension corners. Here $\omega_a$ is the actual strict finite open exchange and $\beta_a$ is its constant-tower open-unit mate. Apply $R_{p_a}^{\mathcal T}$ to this equation and insert the direct-image restriction comparison from Step 1. This supplies a target isomorphism $\kappa_{a,t}$ and the equation $\kappa_{a,t}\operatorname{Res}(\mathscr P_{p_a}\omega_a)=(R_{p_a}^{\mathcal T}\beta_a)\widetilde\kappa_{a,m}$. The middle corner is the one in Step 3: both use $\rho_j$, the canonical reduction/pullback comparison and the unit-preserving scalar/open map. This is also explicit in the transpose comparison of [lem-cbc-completed-open-finite-transpose-coherence]. Completeness and quasi-compactness required by the strict identification hold by Step 2; no extra origin witness is needed for this open factor.

source.place: Tags 03DI and 03DJ, strict finite open-unit transpose identification

proof.text:
By the specified proper/open order in [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map], the strict compact-support map is $w_a=(\mathscr P_{p_a}\omega_a)v'_a$. Substitute the equations of Steps 3 and 4:
$$\kappa_{a,t}\operatorname{Res}(w_a)=(R_{p_a}^{\mathcal T}\beta_a)\widetilde\kappa_{a,m}\operatorname{Res}(v'_a)=(R_{p_a}^{\mathcal T}\beta_a)(E_{p,a}^{\mathcal T}J_j)\kappa_{a,s}=H_a^{\mathcal T}\kappa_{a,s}.$$
The same $\widetilde\kappa_{a,m}$ occurs once and cancels; nothing is inferred from agreement of evaluated morphisms. Naturality follows by composing the natural maps already supplied in Steps 1–4.

source.place: Constituent-compatibility paragraph, compact-support base-change constituent; ordered proper/open assembly

proof.text: Check the corner maps for $a,b,ab$ simultaneously. For the reduction/pullback factors, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-common-quotient-pullback-comparison] gives coherence for identities and composable geometric morphisms, including quotient units and transitions. The tensor factors obey the compositor equation of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. The open factors are normalized to the same open unit on the ringed diagram sites by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]; their constant-tower comparisons obey the successive-base-change equation of [lem-cbc-tower-open-beta-normalization]. Hence the open/reduction part of a composite corner is the successive corner map. For direct-image scalar restriction, the comparisons of Step 1 are the identity on a K-injective diagram and its K-injective restriction. A proper direct image preserves these K-injectives because its left adjoint is exact identified-coefficient inverse image. Thus the two successive direct-image restriction identifications and the composite one are induced by the same underived identity. Their inverse-image counterparts are identified underlying inverse images, with the coefficient compositor fixed in Step 1. Taking their normalized mates preserves composition by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Therefore the $b,d$ maps used in Step 3 intertwine the same compositors; they are not fresh choices for the composite square.

It follows that, when Step 5 is first substituted for $a$ and then for $b$, the target corner for the first substitution is exactly the source corner for the second after the prescribed pullback compositor. Explicitly, any intermediate pair $k,k^{-1}$ contributes $k^{-1}k=1$, so the resulting conjugation has the composite source and target corners verified in Step 6. The constant-tower open and proper maps compose by [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus] and [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. Consequently both successive substitutions use identical intermediate corner maps, as asserted, including the identity base change.

source.place: Constituent-compatibility paragraph, base-change composition; cancellation after the compositor check

proof.text: For a refinement $u:c_1\to c_2$, use its proper/open normalization: its inverse-image arrow is open base change followed by projection to the clopen refinement section. The section projector is identity on that section and zero on its complementary open [lem-cbc-proper-open-clopen-projector]. Scalar restriction leaves these two maps unchanged; open restriction and open extension preserve their specified units and counits by [lem-cbc-ringed-open-scalar-adjunction]. The canonical tensor/open comparisons preserve the same unit on diagram sites [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], so, after the same $z_j$ comparisons, they send this projector to that identical projector. The inverse-image scalar square commutes by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-restriction-pullback-square]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-mate-cube] to these comparisons and the proper adjunctions normalized in Step 1. It sends the strict proper/open refinement mate to $\gamma_{Q_u}$, rather than to an arbitrary isomorphism with its endpoints. Whiskering with $R_{p_2}^{\mathcal T}$ and using the compositor check of Step 6 sends the strict refinement comparison to $C_u=R_{p_2}^{\mathcal T}\gamma_{Q_u}$ (or its inverse for the opposite comparison direction).

source.place: Tags 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose); clopen and scalar-mate refinement in the cited nodes

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-complete-proetale-refinement-exchange-coherence] to $\overline M$, whose evaluations have the supplied finite bounded-below etale-origin witnesses. This gives $C'_{u}H_{a,2}^{\mathcal T}=H_{a,1}^{\mathcal T}G_aC_u$, $C_{vu}=C_uC_v$, $C_1=1$, and the common-refinement cocycle. Replace each $C,H$ by its identified strict map from Steps 5 and 8. At every interior vertex the same corner identification and its inverse cancel (Step 6), so these equations are precisely the strict refinement cocycle and exchange-intertwining equations under $\kappa$. All constructions were made on diagram sites, with their quotient transitions; none used $R\lim$ or faithfulness of evaluations. The coefficient identifications hold for arbitrary scheme maps (Step 1), and the open/proper calculus imposes no $k$-linearity. Hence the argument includes all supplied semilinear maps. For the unrestricted strict refinement identity and composition clauses, apply [lem-cbc-completed-refinement-map-functoriality] on the ambient completed-ring input. Each supplied compactification gives separatedness and local finite type of f. Apply the quotient-reduction functor and conjugate by the supportReduction corners. Functoriality and cancellation of each interior corner give the strict identity and composition equations without finite-origin hypotheses.

The statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to live and side-live, and the item is still unsplit there, so no other group has superseded it. Base-change and coefficient setup: R=O_E is a Noetherian adic datum with finite perfect quotients P_n, and (p,p_a,a,ā) is cartesian by pur713. Step 2: ρ_j and the scalar/open map e give z_j; the extension-by-zero comparison, with j quasi-compact, makes j_!M complete. Step 3: the proper normalization d·Res(v')=E·b holds, and I recomputed its whiskering by z_j using naturality of E. Step 4: the strict mate identification gives b·r(ω)=β·a; its middle corner uses the same open-tensor, constant-completion and unit-preserving comparisons, which the transpose-coherence node fixes. Step 5 is an elementary substitution, w_a=(Pω)v'. Step 6: every compositor piece is cited (common-quotient comparison, cochain tensor coherence, open-tensor normalization, β successive formula, the flat-ringed d as the identity on K-injectives preserved by u_*, and mate pasting). Step 8: the clopen projector is unchanged by restriction, and the ring-restriction square plus the mate cube give C_u=R_{p2}γ_{Q_u} for the actual map. Step 9: the hypothesis of the refinement-coherence node holds because Res R_X(M) at level n is the restriction along O_E→P_n of M_n≅ν^*L_n; its e_i equals H_a and it needs no qcqs condition on the base. Edge cases checked: M=0, a=id, j=id (reduces to the proper normalization), identity refinement, a noncartesian refinement with a nonempty complement, and semilinear maps. No cycle. lem-cbc-complete-proetale-strict-tower-realization is the after-Rlim neighbour, not a duplicate. No SGA citation. Batch-5 flags: lem-trf-right-fraction-dense-subcategory (calculus of fractions), lem-trf-site-functorial-flat-resolution (flat resolutions of module sheaves) and lem-trf-iterated-square-mates (mate/conjugate identity, reached via the beta-normalization and clopen-projector citations) are general category or homological infrastructure, not steps of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so I accept them. I accept the 20 tool_uses as generic infrastructure; the cbc ones are on the unit's route anyway. Advisory: the report says the source pointer was updated to latest, but only proof_origin was.
